title: CSL projection
description: How one source record's JSON becomes a CSL-JSON item: each key is a CSL variable and each value a rule that reads the source record. A source's projection is data, so a new bibliographic source needs a projection, not a script.

path.description: A dot path into the source record. A segment ending in [] maps the rest of the path over an array, so the rule reads an array.

value.description: A constant, for a variable every record of the source shares.

template.description: A string with {path} holes; it yields nothing when any hole reads nothing.

first.description: The first rule that yields a value.

as.description: The CSL value kind the read value becomes.

family.description: names: the key of a name record's family name.

given.description: names: the key of a name record's given name.

literal.description: names: the key of a name record's literal name.

initials.description: names: display strings read as "Family AB", family then initials.

split.description: names, type: the separator a single display string is split on.

aliases.description: type: the source's own type words, lowercased, as CSL types.

prefer.description: type: CSL types chosen first when any of the source's words alias to them.

separator.description: join: the separator between the unique values.
